scheme_name: Scheme for Establishment of Backyard Poultry Units
description:
The Scheme for Establishment of Backyard Poultry Units was launched by the Government of India in 2014. 

This initiative aims to enhance the livelihood of rural households through the promotion of poultry farming. 

The scheme is particularly focused on marginalized and economically weaker sections of society. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to provide financial assistance to eligible beneficiaries for establishing backyard poultry units. 

The target is to establish around 2.5 million backyard poultry units across the country by the year 2025. 

The scheme aims to boost egg production and improve the nutritional status of rural households. 

It also seeks to create self-employment opportunities in rural areas. 

Under this scheme, financial assistance is provided to beneficiaries in the form of a subsidy. 

The subsidy amount is set at 50% of the total cost of establishing the unit. 

For women and Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe beneficiaries, the subsidy is increased to 60%. 

The maximum subsidy amount for each beneficiary is capped at ₹18,000. 

This means that for a unit costing ₹36,000, a beneficiary can receive a subsidy of ₹18,000. 

The scheme encourages the establishment of units with a capacity of 50 to 100 birds. 

It is designed to be implemented through the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying. 

The implementing agency at the state level is the respective State Animal Husbandry Department. 

Eligibility criteria for the scheme include being a resident of a rural area. 

Beneficiaries must belong to a marginalized section of society. 

They should also have a minimum age of 18 years. 

There are no specific educational qualifications required to apply for this scheme. 

However, applicants must demonstrate a basic understanding of poultry farming. 

The application process begins with the submission of an application form to the local Animal Husbandry Department. 

The application form can be obtained from the department's office or downloaded from the official website. 

Applicants must provide documents such as identity proof, address proof, and bank account details. 

A project report detailing the proposed poultry unit may also be required. 

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by the officials of the Animal Husbandry Department. 

If approved, beneficiaries receive a sanction order detailing the subsidy amount. 

The subsidy is disbursed directly to the beneficiary's bank account. 

The timeline for the entire process from application to disbursement can vary. 

Typically, it may take around 30 to 60 days for the approval and disbursement process. 

The scheme is implemented in a phased manner. 

Beneficiaries are encouraged to start their poultry units within three months of receiving the subsidy. 

Regular monitoring and evaluation are conducted by the Animal Husbandry Department. 

This ensures that the beneficiaries are utilizing the funds appropriately. 

The scheme also provides training and capacity-building programs for beneficiaries. 

These programs cover various aspects of poultry farming including management and disease control. 

The training is often conducted by experts from the Animal Husbandry Department or associated organizations. 

The scheme has been instrumental in improving the livelihoods of many rural households. 

It has also contributed to increased egg production in various states. 

As of 2023, the scheme has successfully established over 1 million backyard poultry units. 

This has resulted in a significant increase in local egg production. 

The scheme has also led to improved nutritional intake among rural families. 

The government continues to promote this initiative through awareness campaigns. 

These campaigns aim to educate potential beneficiaries about the benefits of poultry farming. 

The scheme is part of a larger effort to promote self-sufficiency in food production. 

It aligns with the government's vision of doubling farmers' income by 2022. 

The scheme is also linked to various other agricultural and rural development initiatives. 

This includes the National Livestock Mission and the Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana. 

The success of the scheme is measured through various indicators. 

These include the number of units established and the increase in egg production. 

Beneficiaries are also encouraged to form self-help groups for better resource management. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from beneficiaries. 

Many have reported increased income and improved living standards. 

The government is committed to expanding the reach of this scheme. 

Efforts are being made to include more beneficiaries from different states. 

The scheme is expected to evolve with changing needs and challenges in the poultry sector. 

Overall, the Scheme for Establishment of Backyard Poultry Units represents a significant step towards rural empowerment. 

It provides a sustainable source of income and nutrition for rural families. 

The scheme exemplifies the government's commitment to improving the livelihoods of the rural poor. 

For more information, beneficiaries can contact the local Animal Husbandry Department. 

They can also visit the official website for updates and guidelines. 

The scheme continues to play a crucial role in the development of rural poultry farming in India. 

It is a testament to the potential of small-scale farming in contributing to food security. 

The government remains focused on supporting and enhancing this initiative in the coming years.
